question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched control as CCP General Secretary, president, and Central Military Commission chairman underpins the 95% implied probability that he remains in power through 2026. Term limits were removed in 2018, enabling a third term in 2022-2023 and positioning him for continued leadership at the 2027 Party Congress, with no public indications of retirement or rivals emerging. Recent developments, including his active diplomacy with foreign leaders, forward-looking economic planning for the 2026-2030 period, and ongoing military and party consolidation through purges, reinforce trader consensus on stability. Realistic scenarios that could still affect the outcome include sudden health events, an unprecedented internal challenge ahead of the congress, or a major external crisis disrupting elite alignment.

eventMetadata.context_description: A crowded Democratic field remains fluid more than two years before the 2028 primaries, with no prohibitive frontrunner after the party's 2024 loss. Trader consensus prices Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez highest amid progressive momentum and battleground polling gains, followed closely by Gavin Newsom's California governance profile and Jon Ossoff's Georgia Senate fundraising and positioning. National surveys often show Kamala Harris ahead on name recognition, yet markets assign lower odds consistent with historical patterns where early polling leaders fade. The recently approved DNC primary calendar, starting in South Carolina and emphasizing diverse states, along with 2026 midterm results, could shift probabilities by testing candidates on turnout, endorsements, and coalition building across swing-state voting blocs.
